talbot-lace-index: William Henry Fox Talbot, *Lace*, c. 1844 — an index: made by direct contact with the thing itself
deer-mandala: *Deer Mandala of the Kasuga Shrine*, 15th century — a symbol: it means by convention alone

whittier-classroom: Frances Benjamin Johnston, *English Literature — Lesson on Whittier*, Hampton Institute, 1899

lincoln-mcclellan: Alexander Gardner, *Lincoln and McClellan at Antietam*, 1862 — the photo-op is older than the word
folies-bergere: Édouard Manet, *A Bar at the Folies-Bergère*, 1882 — who is looking at whom? the mirror refuses to agree
cahun-gaze: Claude Cahun, *Self-Portrait*, 1920 — a look sent back: the gaze refused
rivera-self-portrait: Diego Rivera, *Self-Portrait*, 1907 — the maker examining himself
good-glass-of-beer: Édouard Manet, *A Good Glass of Beer*, 1873 — gratification, personified

lindbergh-1927: Underwood & Underwood, *Charles Lindbergh*, 1927 — the first global media event: one man, every channel

the-magpie: Claude Monet, *The Magpie*, 1869 — winter light, and the quiet after
duchamp-fountain: Marcel Duchamp, *Fountain*, 1917. The object that made looking insufficient
weems-kitchen-table: Carrie Mae Weems, from *The Kitchen Table Series*, 1990. One table, one light, the whole argument

venus-of-urbino: Titian, *Venus of Urbino*, 1534. What does it ask you to accept as natural?
olympia: Édouard Manet, *Olympia*, 1863. Every refusal is findable in the paint
le-gras: Joseph Nicéphore Niépce, *View from the Window at Le Gras*, 1826. The first photograph, and eight hours of light
wheatfield-crows: Vincent van Gogh, *Wheatfield with Crows*, 1890. Berger's demonstration: the painting, then the painting with a caption

venus-and-mars: Sandro Botticelli, *Venus and Mars*, c. 1485. Berger's cropping demonstration

toystory-disruption: *Toy Story* (1995), stage 2. Disruption: Buzz arrives and displaces Woody

toystory-repair: *Toy Story* (1995), stage 4. Repair: lost in Sid's house, working the way back
toystory-new-equilibrium: *Toy Story* (1995), stage 5. New equilibrium: the rivals, now a pair

goodfellas-copacabana-2: *Goodfellas* (1990). The same unbroken shot, through the service corridor
goodfellas-copacabana-3: *Goodfellas* (1990). One continuous move, ending at the table

ad-sauvage: Dior, *Sauvage*. Full face, direct address, landscape, subject as agent
ad-jadore: Dior, *J'adore*. Gold, averted eyes, the body as surface
nationwide-title: *Nationwide* (BBC). The broadcast on which Morley tested differential readings
rosler-kitchen: Martha Rosler, *Semiotics of the Kitchen*, 1975. A kitchen turned into an alphabet of rage
warhol-brillo: Andy Warhol, *Brillo Boxes*, 1964. The object Danto wrote 'The Artworld' about
goodbye-to-language: Jean-Luc Godard, *Goodbye to Language*, 2014. An image that refuses to add up

edmw-dinner: Ang Lee, *Eat Drink Man Woman*, 1994. The Sunday dinner, where the rules get enforced
bearden-block: Romare Bearden, *The Block*, 1971. Six panels, one street, cut and reassembled
hoch-kitchen-knife: Hannah Höch, *Cut with the Kitchen Knife*, 1919
bird-concert: Frans Snyders, *Bird Concert*, c. 1630. A score hung in a tree and twenty open beaks: a picture you hear before you read it

vandeelen-interior: Dirck van Deelen, *Distinguished Dinner Company in an Interior*, 1631. Architecture, costume, properties and placing: every element decided before anyone speaks

weems-triptych-2: Carrie Mae Weems, second frame. The camera has not moved; only the people have, and the story has already turned
weems-triptych-3: Carrie Mae Weems, third frame. The cut is what happens between frames, never inside one
